title: Research
content: Current Research Themes Knowledge infrastructure is only visible when it fails. Metadata errors erase scholarship. Computational tools locked behind programming expertise exclude entire professional communities. My research sits at the intersection of computational methods and information infrastructure, studying how knowledge gets organized, and accessed. My research addresses three connected areas: Accessible and Accountable Research Tools Powerful methods are of limited use when researchers cannot access them or inspect how they work. I ask how tools can support people with different levels of technical experience while keeping researchers involved in consequential decisions. OpenCoder, an AI assisted open tool for qualitative research in development, is part of this work, alongside my earlier work on Coconut Libtool. Data Documentation and Responsible Reuse Data can travel far beyond the project in which it was created. Without clear documentation, later users may miss how it was collected, categorized, or intended to be used. My work on data documentation asks what researchers need to know about a dataset to interpret and reuse it responsibly. Additionally, I examine where metadata, open datasets, and classification systems introduce errors or encode inequities that affect the communities they describe. title: Home
content: Manika Lamba Assistant Professor, University of Oklahoma Knowledge Infrastructure Human-Computer Interactions Social Computing Critical AI Studies I am an Assistant Professor in the School of Library & Information Studies at the University of Oklahoma. Before joining the University of Oklahoma, I was a Postdoctoral Research Associate at the HathiTrust Research Center in the School of Information Sciences, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. My research sits at the intersection of knowledge organization, social computing, and critical AI studies. I examine how knowledge is organized, represented, discovered, and accessed across scholarly and digital information systems. I use large language models, natural language processing, and machine learning alongside user-centered methods to study how people create, share, and encounter knowledge through digital platforms and to develop more inclusive, and accessible information systems. My research has received support from the University of Oklahoma, Princeton University, National Science Foundation through a microgrant and the Innovation Corps (I-Corps), Association for Information Science and Technology (ASIS&T), and Summer Institutes in Computational Social Science (SICSS). title: Mentorship
content: Mentorship Interested in working with me? Please read this before reaching out to me. I have multiple openings for Fall 2027 for Ph.D. in iSchool. Apply to the Ph.D. in Information Studies at the University of Oklahoma and list Dr. Manika Lamba as a faculty advisor. More details here. Final Deadline: January 15, 2027 I also welcome research assistants and collaborations. Positions begin as early as Spring 2027. Existing graduate and undergraduate students at OU are welcome to join as research assistants. You can apply to conduct research for credit. Students/researchers from outside OU are welcome to join as research collaborators. Funded opportunities are not available at the moment. Before reaching out, please ask yourself: Is this a research question I would be excited to spend several months working on? Everyone’s time is limited, and I want students in my lab to feel proud of the projects they take on — the kind of work you would be happy to share with peers or even people outside the field. title: Software
content: ## Software and Data Software: Coconut Libtool Website Git Paper Authors: M. Lamba and F.A. Santosa Textual analysis remains challenging for researchers, students and practitioners without programming expertise, creating barriers in social sciences and humanities research. This poster presents Coconut Libtool 2.0, an enhanced web-based application that makes advanced textual analysis and visualization accessible to everyone. Building upon version 1.0, Coconut Libtool 2.0 significantly expands data source integration to include HathiTrust digital library, Dimensions, and PubMed, alongside existing Scopus, Web of Science, Lens, and customized file support. Enhanced text and visualization techniques include established methods for topic modeling, network text analysis, and keyword stemming, in addition to new features such as burst detection, sentiment analysis, and scattertext visualization.
